notes: Main result (paper-closest row = raw ciphertext): plaintext BLEU=69.87 (95% CI [61.98975606735502, 78.172992683851]) -> CAPRISE raw BLEU=13.7 (95% CI [9.72372181194507, 17.48354429712425]; -80.4%); the stronger scale-normalising attacker reaches BLEU=34.58 (95% CI [27.910914357781962, 40.91128454180229]; still below plaintext; privacy upper bound, F3/A11). Paper Table II: 83.021 -> 12.425. N=50.

F14 (critical): Vec2Text gtr-base inverts vec2text-convention embeddings (T5 mean-pool, no Dense, no L2 normalisation, norms ~0.5-1.0); the M0 sentence-transformers GTR embeddings give garbage even without encryption. The gate audits that convention via saved arrays + recorded norms.

Bootstrap 95% CI: passage-level nonparametric bootstrap, 1000 resamples, fixed seed 20260101; the gate recomputes the CI (and per-passage components) from the stored hypotheses + references in this environment and requires an exact match.

Step/beam sensitivity (F6/A11): the same 5 passages were re-run at num_steps=50, sequence_beam_width=10 in all three modes; the 20/4 baseline is recomputed on exactly the same 5 passages from the 50-passage run. The Lead reduced the sensitivity sample from 10 to 5 because the shared machine was loaded (loadavg ~5-7); this is a scope adjustment (direction/magnitude only), not a threshold relaxation. The gate requires the deltas and the config, not a particular sign (the paper states neither setting).

The absolute difference from paper Table II is reported, not fitted: the paper does not state num_steps / beam width / N / per-passage length (A11) and uses an A100; our MPS-feasible settings are recorded in the artefact and explained in notes/exp3_vec2text.md. No gate threshold was relaxed relative to the 10-passage main experiment; coverage was extended (N>=50, CI, 50/10 sensitivity on 5 passages).
This gate validates the committed artefact and recomputes the metric + CI + encryption-audit layer in the calling environment (vec2text inversion itself is not re-run).
